still: A photorealistic wide frame of a draughty church-hall community room, taken from a lens bolted high in one corner near the ceiling and angled down, so the people are small and seen from above. Brandon sits on a stacked-plastic folding chair in the lower left third, leaning over his phone with his brows lifted, his eyelids wide and the corners of his mouth pulled up, his eyes aimed at the phone in his hands; the phone's face is turned away from the lens and shows only a pale smear of light on his chin. Behind him, three campaigners in anoraks and jumpers lean over a trestle table covered in paper cups and loose leaflets, one reaching for a roll of masking tape. The only light is a row of buzzing fluorescent tubes on the ceiling and a grey daylight smear through a high frosted window, so the colours are washed out and slightly green, with soft compression blocks, fine night-mode noise and slightly blown highlights near the window. Shot on a cheap fixed wide-angle sensor with a little barrel distortion, nothing in frame carries any writing. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. In the draughty hall, Brandon on the folding chair stares at his phone and breaks into a slow delighted grin as a glow brightens against his chin, while the campaigners behind him keep sorting papers at the trestle table. Later in the eight seconds Brandon shifts his weight on the chair and glances up towards the table without turning his head. One fluorescent tube flickers faintly overhead. The compressed, washed-out picture keeps its fine grain, shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Audio: a flickering tube's buzz, the squeak of a plastic chair, paper rustling, a roll of tape unpeeling, distant traffic through the window. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photorealistic mid-wide frame of the same church-hall room, taken by a phone propped on a shelf against a breeze-block wall at about head height and a little off to one side, with the lens slightly smudged. Brandon stands on the left of the frame holding his phone out at arm's length towards Jenny, with raised brows, bright wide eyelids and a proud half-open smile, his eyes on her face; the phone's screen faces away from the lens and shows only a blurred patch of light. Jenny stands on the right of the frame behind a trestle table with a heap of stapled papers, her head tilted down at the papers, brows drawn together, her eyes aimed at the page and not at him. A tea urn and a stack of beige cups sit on a hatch counter behind them. The light is flat strip lighting from the ceiling plus a cold daylight patch from a side door, giving a washed-out, slightly milky picture with visible compression noise. No writing appears anywhere in frame. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon on the left pushes his phone slightly closer to Jenny on the right and beams at her, while Jenny keeps squaring and stapling her pile of papers, glancing at his hand for only a moment. Later in the eight seconds Brandon's smile slips a fraction and his arm lowers a few centimetres as Jenny turns a page. Steam drifts up from the tea urn in the background. The phone's smudged lens leaves a soft halo around the bright patch by the side door. The camera does not move. Audio: the tick of a stapler, paper sliding on a wooden table, the hiss of the urn, a shoe scuffing on lino. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photorealistic wide frame of a council planning meeting in a municipal chamber with a low ceiling, seen from a lens fixed on a wall bracket in the far corner, looking diagonally across the room. Rows of grey-upholstered chairs fill the foreground, holding a scatter of residents in coats and fleeces with their backs mostly to the lens. At a long veneer table on the right side of the room sits Gary, clearly visible in a suit jacket with a lanyard hanging down his chest, his head bent, brows level, eyelids half lowered and his eyes aimed at the papers in front of him; a laminated name card stands on the table with its face turned away. Beside him sit two councillors with water jugs. The light is flat ceiling panels plus a dim window with the blinds half drawn, giving a washed-out, slightly yellow picture with low resolution and soft compression smearing. No readable text anywhere. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Gary at the developer's table turns a page of his papers with one finger and keeps reading, while the councillor beside him pours a glass of water. Later in the eight seconds Gary lifts his eyes towards the rows of residents for a moment, then lowers them again. A ceiling panel hums with a very faint flicker. A resident in the front row shifts in a chair. The camera does not move. Audio: the clink of a water jug on a glass, paper turning, a cough in the rows of chairs, the low buzz of a ceiling panel. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photorealistic wide frame of the community hall after everyone has gone, taken from a lens mounted high above the stage and looking down the length of the room, so the two figures are small. Jenny stands on the left of the frame stacking folding chairs against a breeze-block wall, shoulders dropped, brows pulled together, eyelids heavy and her eyes aimed at the floor in front of her. Brandon stands on the right of the frame a few metres away with his hands open at his sides, brows tilted up in the middle, lips pressed and pulled slightly down, his eyes aimed at Jenny; a small warm patch of light glows at his jeans pocket. The floor is scuffed pale lino scattered with paper cups, and the only light is a few remaining ceiling tubes and a dull orange streetlight leaking through a high window. The colour is washed out and muddy, with night-mode grain and compression blocks in the dark corners. Nothing in frame has any writing. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Jenny on the left lifts a folding chair onto a growing stack and wipes her palm down her trousers, while Brandon on the right takes one small step towards her with his mouth moving softly. Later in the eight seconds Jenny turns slightly away from him towards the wall and Brandon looks down at his own pocket as the warm glow pulses once. A single ceiling tube flickers in the far corner. The camera does not move. Audio: metal chair legs clinking together, a long scuff of shoes on lino, a distant radiator ticking, a faint low phone buzz. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photorealistic frame of a low-quality handheld phone video in a cheap gym, the lens held at arm's length and tilted slightly sideways, with a fleshy thumb covering the bottom-right corner of the lens in a soft pink blur. Brandon fills the left half of the frame in close-up, too near the lens, with raised brows, bright wide eyelids and a broad open-mouthed grin, his eyes aimed straight into the lens. Far behind him on the right, small and slightly out of focus, Gary is walking towards a fire-exit door with a lanyard showing around his neck, head turned away from the lens. Rubber floor tiles, a rack of mismatched dumbbells, a mirror with a crack and a ceiling of exposed ducting recede behind them. The light is harsh overhead strip tubes that blow out the highlights on Brandon's forehead, with a bluish cast, heavy compression artefacts and oversharpened edges. No writing or numbers appear in frame. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon in the left foreground nods and grins at the lens, his mouth moving without forming clear words, while far behind him Gary keeps edging towards the fire-exit door at the right of frame. Later in the eight seconds Gary reaches the door and puts a hand on the bar as Brandon's grin widens slightly and his eyes stay on the lens. A strip tube overhead gives a slow flicker. The thumb stays fixed at the corner of the lens. The camera does not move. Audio: the thump of music through a gym wall, a distant treadmill belt, rubber soles squeaking on the floor, the clunk of a dumbbell being set down. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photorealistic head-and-shoulders frame taken by the built-in lens at the top edge of a laptop screen, looking slightly up at a home-office desk. Giles sits centred and a little low in the frame, his brows drawn very slightly together, his eyelids narrowed and his lips pressed flat, his eyes aimed down at something below the lens; one hand holds a fork stopped in the air a short distance from his mouth with a green forkful of salad on it. Behind him a tall bookcase of mismatched hardbacks, a framed print and a lamp fill the wall; the book spines are soft and unreadable. Cold white daylight pours from a window out of frame on the right and blows out part of the wall, while the face falls into dull flat shadow on the left. Washed-out colour, soft focus, a visibly compressed video-call picture with smeared skin detail. A takeaway salad tub sits on the desk edge. No writing anywhere. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Giles frowns very slightly at the screen below the lens, his fork frozen in the air, then slowly lowers the fork back to the tub. Later in the eight seconds he blinks once and his eyes flick a few degrees to the right. A lamp on the bookcase shimmers faintly as the compression crawls. The camera does not move. Audio: a quiet room tone, a plastic fork scraping a tub, the soft click of a trackpad, a distant car passing outside. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photorealistic frame taken by a tablet propped against a stack of books on a kitchen counter, looking up at the person from below at a slight angle. Giles stands at the counter in the middle of the frame, a plastic bowl of salad in one hand and the other hand held low with a thumb tapping a phone out of sight, his head already turned to the left so that his eyes aim away from the lens, brows level and mouth closed. Behind him are cream kitchen cabinets, a kettle, a tea towel on an oven handle and a pinboard with blurred papers. The light is a single bright ceiling spotlight directly above him that leaves his eye sockets in shadow, plus a blue-grey cast from a window. The picture is washed out, noisy, slightly soft, and compressed so that edges blur and block in the dark areas. No writing, numbers or interface are visible. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Giles at the counter lifts a forkful of salad and his thumb taps once on the phone in his other hand without his looking down. Later in the eight seconds he shifts his weight onto his other foot and his gaze drifts further away to the left. The kettle behind him ticks faintly as it cools. The camera does not move. Audio: a fork on the rim of a plastic bowl, one soft phone tap, a kettle ticking, a fridge compressor humming. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photorealistic high-angle wide frame of a cheap basement gym, taken from a lens fixed up in a corner of the ceiling and tilted steeply down, so the two men are small and seen from above. Brandon lies on his back on a padded bench in the lower centre, his brows lifted, his eyelids soft and wide, the corners of his mouth up in a trusting half-smile, his eyes aimed up at Gary; a heavily loaded barbell rests above his chest on the rack. Gary stands at the head of the bench, bending a little, both hands under the bar, brows level and his eyes aimed down at Brandon. The floor is black rubber matting, a rack of dumbbells and a rolled yoga mat sit against a breeze-block wall, and the light is two buzzing strip tubes plus a dim bulb that leave the corners murky. The colour is washed out with a faint green cast, strong compression smear and night-mode grain. No writing anywhere in frame. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. In the gym, Brandon on the bench keeps looking up at Gary with a trusting smile while Gary at the head of the bench holds both hands steady under the bar. Later in the eight seconds Gary's eyes flick briefly towards the door on the far wall and back down, and Brandon's chest rises with a slow breath. One strip tube flickers overhead. The camera does not move. Audio: the buzz of a strip tube, a slow exhale, a bench pad creaking, a muffled treadmill from the next room. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photorealistic closer frame from the same high corner of the ceiling of the cheap basement gym, looking steeply down, tighter than before so that Gary's torso and the head of the bench fill the frame. Gary stands over the head of the bench with his two hands under a loaded barbell, his fingers just beginning to open, his brows slack, his eyelids half lowered and his mouth loose and still, his eyes aimed straight down and empty. Below him on the bench only the top of Brandon's head and his raised hands can be seen at the bottom of the frame. The rubber matting around them is scuffed and grey. Light comes from two buzzing strip tubes and a dim bulb, giving washed-out, slightly green colour, soft compression blocks and coarse grain. No writing anywhere in frame. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Gary's fingers loosen very slightly under the bar and his face stays blank as he looks down; the bar stays where it is. Later in the eight seconds his shoulders rise on an inhale and his eyes stay fixed on the bench beneath him. A strip tube overhead flickers once. The camera does not move. Audio: a strip tube buzzing, a slow breath, the faint creak of a bench pad, the quiet hiss of a fan in the corner. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photorealistic wide frame of a small, hard-surfaced coroner's examination room, taken from a lens on a wall bracket above the door and looking down across the room. A stainless steel table stands in the centre of the frame with a body under a white sheet, and a pair of scuffed trainers with dark stained soles hangs out of the end of the sheet. Giles stands beside the table on the right of the frame in a navy gilet, his head slightly lowered and his brows drawn together, one finger pressed to his ear and his lips moving as though speaking quietly into the air, his eyes aimed at the floor. Pale tiled walls, a steel sink, a wall clock with blank hands and a trolley of covered trays recede behind him. The light is hard fluorescent strip light with cold green-white reflections on the steel, producing a washed-out picture with compression blocks, grain and slightly blown highlights on the table. No readable writing or numbers anywhere in frame. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Giles beside the steel table keeps one finger pressed to his ear and his lips move softly without forming clear words, while his gaze stays on the floor. Later in the eight seconds he shifts his weight onto his other foot and his eyes lift briefly to the white sheet before dropping again. A fluorescent tube flickers faintly over the sink. The camera does not move. Audio: the buzz of a fluorescent tube, a refrigeration unit humming, the squeak of a rubber sole on tile, a slow drip from the sink. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.
